title: start_run does not record wall-clock start time in RunState or prompt context
description: start_run captures a compact timestamp (e.g. 20260612T214227Z) to construct run_file_path but never stores it in RunState and never injects an ISO 8601 wall_start_time token into the run prompt. The agent must reconstruct the start time by parsing the filename, which is fragile and has been observed to produce guessed or incorrect timestamps in the emitted run JSON artifact.
proposed_resolution: 1. Add wall_start_time: Option<chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>> to RunState and a set_wall_start_time() setter. 2. In start_run::execute(), call chrono::Utc::now() once, store it in RunState via state.lock().unwrap().set_wall_start_time(now), and inject it into the prompt as {{wall_start_time}} in RFC 3339 format. 3. Add {{wall_start_time}} to the Session context block in src/prompts/run.prompt alongside run_id. 4. Surface it in get_run_status output so the agent can reference it without parsing the filename.
